question: What is the difference between an array and a pointer?

scenes.sub: Arrays decay into pointers. They are not pointers.
scenes.say: Array versus pointer. People often say an array is just a pointer. It isn't. It decays into one, and that difference shows up in interviews all the time.

scenes.head: Storage vs. an address
scenes.say: An array is the elements themselves: five ints, side by side, twenty bytes. No address is stored anywhere. A pointer is a separate variable that holds an address, eight bytes on a sixty four bit system. When you use arr in an expression, it decays to a pointer to its first element. But size of arr is twenty, while size of p is eight. And p can move, p plus one points to the next element, while arr itself can never be reassigned.

scenes.head: The classic trap: arrays as parameters
scenes.say: The classic trap. Passing an array to a function decays it too. Even if you write int a of five, the parameter is really an int pointer. So size of a inside the function gives eight, not twenty. The size is lost. To keep it, pass the length separately, take the array by reference with a template, or better, use s t d colon colon array or s t d colon colon span.

scenes.head: Side by side
scenes.say: An array is storage. A pointer is an address. The size of operator on an array gives all its bytes, on a pointer just eight. Arrays can't be assigned, pointers can be re-pointed. Taking the ampersand of an array gives a pointer to the whole array, a different type. And an array knows its size, because it's part of its type. A pointer doesn't.

lines: An array IS the elements; a pointer just holds an address.
Arrays decay to &arr[0] in most expressions, and as function parameters.
So sizeof, & and assignment differ. Prefer std::array or std::span.
scenes.say: An array is the elements themselves. A pointer just holds an address. Arrays decay to a pointer to their first element in most expressions, including when passed to functions. That's why size of, ampersand, and assignment behave differently. In modern code, prefer s t d colon colon array or span.
